messages:
nisha_fin: Heads-up - finance noticed ~75 invoices with an unexpected credit memo line from this morning's sync. NetSuite shows a credit on the invoice but Stripe charge has no refund.

greg_recon: Can you share an example invoice id? I'll pull the ledger.

nisha_fin: INV-2026-3321. In NetSuite there's a Credit Memo (CM-7889) applied for $12 platform fee. We never issued refunds.

aina_eng: Interesting. I searched the webhook logs and found a 409 conflict from NetSuite API during the initial sync for some invoices. Our retry path creates a new fee adjustment record locally and then reposts it to NetSuite, which results in an extra credit memo.

kyle_ops: Do we return the proper idempotency-key to NetSuite when we retry? The connector should include our sync_id to be idempotent.

aina_eng: For most flows we set X-Sync-ID, but the connector had a bug where the header was omitted for 502 backoff retries (we only set it for the first attempt). That explains why NetSuite accepted the retry as a fresh request and created CM.

greg_recon: Ok that matches: duplicate local adjustment + successful retry push => orphan CM in NetSuite. How many already posted?

nisha_fin: Initial scan shows 75 invoices with posted CM entries, total impact ~$900. I can attach CSV.

aina_eng: Mitigation plan: 1) Patch connector to always attach X-Sync-ID on retries (hotfix). 2) Pause netsuite_sync to stop more postings. 3) Flag local duplicate adjustments so sync ignores them. 4) Produce NetSuite reversal JE CSV for accounting to post.

kyle_ops: Pausing sync now. @netsuite-bot pause netsuite_sync.

netsuite-bot: Action: netsuite_sync paused by kyle_ops at 2026-03-25T08:40:12Z.

greg_recon: For detection, use this query to find likely duplicates (group by invoice + fee_amount + sync_id nulls):

```sql
WITH candidates AS (
  SELECT id, invoice_id, fee_cents, sync_id, created_at,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY invoice_id, fee_cents ORDER BY created_at) rn
  FROM invoice_adjustments
  WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '10 days'
)
SELECT id, invoice_id, fee_cents FROM candidates WHERE rn > 1;
```

nisha_fin: Perfect. I'll review and then request NetSuite reversals for those already posted. Finance wants the CSV with original CM ids and our sync_id (if present) for audit.

aina_eng: Hotfix timeline: small change in connector to persist X-Sync-ID on every attempt, add tests for retry header, push in 45m. Also will add a pre-send check: if an adjustment for invoice_id + fee_cents + sync_id exists, don't create new adjustment.

greg_recon: For cleanup, I'd prefer marking duplicates with a 'needs_net_reversal' flag instead of outright deleting. Then accounting can review. Example update script: INSERT INTO adjustment_reversal_candidates (adjustment_id, reason, detected_by) SELECT id, 'duplicate_sync', 'auto-detect' FROM (the query above);

nisha_fin: That works. Also please include mapping of CM ids in the CSV so accounting can reverse exact JE posted.

kyle_ops: After hotfix deploy, we'll do a dry-run of sync against a sandbox NetSuite instance to confirm idempotency behavior before resuming production.

aina_eng: Agreed. Adding an integration test that simulates NetSuite 502 then replay and asserts only one CM created.

nisha_fin: Please include an executive note with root cause (missing X-Sync-ID on retries), impact (# invoices, $ amount), mitigation steps, and timeline so I can brief accounting and ops.

greg_recon: I'll attach the discovery CSV in ~20m and tag FIN-820 for the connector fix and FIN-821 for the reversal work.

nisha_fin: Thanks all. React if you see this and I'll coordinate sign-off with accounting. :white_check_mark:

aina_eng: :white_check_mark:

greg_recon: :thumbsup:
